issue: May the government use a defendant's post-arrest, pre-Miranda silence as substantive evidence of guilt in its case-in-chief?

sides.position: The government may use a defendant's post-arrest, pre-Miranda silence as direct evidence of guilt in its case-in-chief (the Eleventh Circuit's rule under Rivera).
cases: United States v. Rivera, 944 F.2d 1563 (11th Cir. 1991)
United States v. Wilchcombe, 838 F.3d 1179 (11th Cir. 2016)
United States v. Cabezas-Montano, 949 F.3d 567 (11th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: Contrary position, which the opinion describes as the rule in other circuits. The excerpts do not name those circuits or cases.

this_court: The Eleventh Circuit follows its own precedent in Rivera and permits the use of post-arrest, pre-Miranda silence as substantive evidence of guilt.
quote: Palacios-Solis points out a circuit split on this issue.
cite: United States v. Trinity Rolando Cabezas-Montano, 949 F.3d 567 (11th Cir. 2020)
